sections.title: 听力 A · 1—4
sections.transcript:
W: Helen, are you still following that exercise video every morning?
M: No. The movements became faster in week three, and my old knee injury started hurting. I assumed stopping meant I had failed.
W: What did the physiotherapist say?
M: She said pain was information, not a test of character. She recommended the gentle class in Green Park and told me to mention the injury to the instructor.
W: Isn't the park class for complete beginners?
M: It welcomes them, but everyone receives a harder or easier version of each movement. Yesterday I used a chair for balance while two experienced members exercised without one.
W: Do you miss exercising at home?
M: I miss choosing my own time. The park class starts at seven thirty, even in light rain. But the instructor corrects my position, which the video cannot do.
W: What is your goal now?
M: Three comfortable sessions a week for the next month. I used to count only difficult minutes. Now I measure progress by whether I can return without pain.

options: Helen can choose any start time.
The instructor can correct her position.
questions.explanation: 真人教练能纠正姿势。

questions.prompt: How will Helen measure progress?
questions.explanation: 新目标是规律且无痛地完成训练。

sections.title: 听力 A · 5—8
sections.transcript: Jacob used to visit the farmers' market every Saturday morning. He liked meeting growers, but finding a parking space often took half an hour. Because the trip felt difficult, he bought large boxes of vegetables to avoid returning soon. Some food inevitably spoiled. This spring, six farmers opened a Wednesday collection point at a neighbourhood café. Customers order online by Monday and choose a small, medium or family box. Jacob selected the family box first because its price per kilogram was lowest. After weighing what he threw away, he changed to the small one. It costs slightly more per item, yet his total weekly spending has fallen. Collection takes five minutes on his walk home. The boxes contain whatever is ready on local farms, so customers cannot choose every vegetable. A recipe card helps with less familiar produce. Jacob still goes to the Saturday market occasionally, especially when friends visit. The new service has not replaced the pleasure of the market. It has simply made fresh food fit an ordinary working week and taught him that value depends on use, not package size.

questions.explanation: 单件略贵但浪费少，周总支出下降。

options: They are available only to farmers.

questions.explanation: 内容随农场当季产出，不能逐项选择。

sections.title: 听力 A · 9—12
sections.transcript: Welcome to the River Walk programme. Last year everyone followed the same five-kilometre route, but this separated faster walkers from people who needed rests. From Sunday, we will offer two groups. The steady group leaves the sports centre at nine and follows the full riverside path. The gentle group departs ten minutes later, uses a shorter route and stops at three benches. Both groups meet at the café at ten thirty, so friends can begin at different speeds and still finish together. Please choose your group when you arrive; you do not need to decide in advance. Walk leaders carry water for emergencies, but participants should bring their own drink and wear shoes suitable for uneven ground. Heavy rain will move the activity to the covered market, where we will do stretching and balance exercises. Check the programme's message page after eight on Sunday morning if the weather is uncertain. The walks remain free. A local clinic has supplied reflective bands, and we ask everyone to return these at the café rather than take them home.

questions.prompt: What should walkers do with the reflective bands?
questions.explanation: 要求在终点咖啡馆归还。

sections.title: 听力 A · 13—16
sections.transcript: When our apartment building created a roof garden, the first drawing showed rows of colourful flowers. Residents liked the picture, but several asked whether the limited space could also produce something useful. The final plan mixed flowers for insects with herbs that people could pick. The real difficulty was not choosing plants. It was remembering to water them. A long list of volunteers looked impressive, yet people assumed someone else would go upstairs. During a hot weekend, three containers dried out. We replaced the list with a board showing one name for each morning and evening. Volunteers now photograph the watered containers and post the picture in a small group. This is evidence that the task is complete, not a competition for attractive photographs. We also moved the water barrel away from the roof edge after a safety inspection. The garden produced enough mint for a building picnic, although not enough vegetables for meals. Its greatest success may be social: neighbours who previously passed silently on the stairs now exchange short messages about weather, bees and whose turn comes next.

options: Residents wanted plants they could use.
questions.explanation: 居民希望有限空间也种植可使用的东西。

options: The roof was closed all week.
questions.explanation: 志愿者名单过长，大家以为别人会浇水。

questions.explanation: 照片用于确认任务完成。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker see as the garden's greatest benefit?
options: It supplies every household with food.
questions.explanation: 结尾强调邻居间开始交流。

sections.title: 听力 A · 17—20
sections.transcript: I had cycled for years, so I expected the road-safety course to feel unnecessary. Then the instructor asked us to signal while looking behind us. I turned my whole bicycle and crossed the painted line. Instead of taking us into traffic, she kept the group on an empty sports ground. We practised the movement slowly between cones until everyone could travel straight. The next exercise involved opening car doors. One learner sat in a parked car while cyclists watched how suddenly the door entered their path. This felt artificial at first, but it helped us understand why riding too close to parked vehicles is dangerous. Rain began before the planned road ride. I assumed the lesson would end, yet we moved under a covered stand and discussed three routes using a map. The shortest route included a difficult roundabout; the safest added four minutes. I chose the longer one when I cycled home. The course did not teach me to pedal faster. It revealed habits I had stopped noticing and gave me a controlled place to replace them.

questions.prompt: What was the main value of the course for the speaker?
questions.explanation: 课程让他发现并改掉已经忽视的习惯。

sections.title: 听力 B · 21—25
sections.transcript: The Healthy Cooking Programme was launched in 2022 after residents asked for affordable meal classes. It meets every Thursday evening in the training kitchen at South College, from 6:30 until 8:00. The yearly charge is twelve pounds, though students under eighteen pay nothing. To register, collect a blue form from reception and provide one photograph. New members may take home two pieces of kitchen equipment during their first month; after that they can borrow four. The main annual workshop takes place in October and explains safe food storage. It is suitable for people who have never cooked independently. Arrive by 6:20, since the external door cannot be opened after the lesson begins. Maya Chen coordinates the programme and answers course questions directly. The college's general office only manages rooms. Each class uses low-cost ingredients, and a portion guide prevents learners buying more than a recipe requires. Participants may exchange recipes, but they must label borrowed containers and return them at the following session. Clear routines make healthy cooking easier to continue at home. Every lesson ends with a ten-minute cleaning routine. Participants may keep the recipe sheet, while knives and measuring equipment must remain in the kitchen. Allergies should be reported when booking.

sections.title: 阅读 A · 26—30
sections.text:
When Daniel first became involved with the riverside path, the plan was to add more exercise signs. The early suggestion seemed workable and attracted early support. Observation during the trial showed that evening users could not see uneven surfaces clearly. The underlying aim still had value. It showed that the organisers had understood the goal more clearly than the daily experience of the people expected to take part.

The team therefore decided to improve lighting and resting places. They also agreed to install benches at regular intervals. During the following month, participation increased and fewer people asked staff for emergency help. A set of small revisions, rather than costly equipment, produced the improvement.

The evidence had clear limits. The revised system did not suit everyone, and the organisers continued to offer an alternative. They also avoided treating the first month's increase as final proof. Seasonal habits and publicity could both affect the figures.

The most serious difficulty was that older walkers avoided the longest section. Rather than insisting on the draft, Daniel invited users to describe exactly when and why the difficulty occurred. Their answers were more useful than a simple satisfaction score. Some people valued convenience, others needed clear instructions, and several wanted enough time to become familiar with the change.

In the organiser’s view, the lasting lesson was simple: design should respond to how and when people use a place. A project can sound excellent in a meeting and still create unnecessary barriers in practice. Careful observation gives people a chance to improve an idea without abandoning its purpose. It also makes success easier to define: not as perfect agreement, but as a service that more people can use with confidence. The experience also reminded those involved that small practical details can strongly influence whether a good idea works. Rather than making quick claims, the organisers continued to collect comments and adjust the project carefully. Motion sensors will measure evening use without identifying individuals, while maintenance reports distinguish lighting faults from complaints about the path surface.

options: Evening users could not see uneven surfaces clearly.
questions.explanation: 第一段明确说明试行暴露出的情况。

options: They asked users for detailed accounts.
questions.explanation: 第二段说明邀请使用者描述困难发生的时间和原因。

options: Participation rose and urgent requests fell.
questions.explanation: 第三段直接给出参与增加、紧急求助减少。

options: No one had used the service.
questions.explanation: 第四段指出季节和宣传也会影响数字。

questions.prompt: What broader lesson did the path project offer?
options: Change succeeds when practical needs are understood.
All public projects should follow one fixed model.

sections.title: 阅读 A · 31—35
sections.text:
At the point when Priya started working on the air-quality programme, the stated objective involved publish one monthly average. Initially, the proposal looked convincing and attracted early support. Evidence gathered during testing demonstrated that a single figure hid changes near school travel times. That finding did not destroy the purpose of the scheme. It showed that the coordinators had understood the goal more clearly than the daily experience of the residents expected to take part.

Even so, the figures were not conclusive. The revised system did not suit everyone, and the coordinators kept another option available. Nor did they regard the first month's increase as final proof. Weather, calendars and publicity could influence the figures.

The most serious barrier was that technical labels confused many parents. The coordinator chose not to defend the original design, Priya invited users to describe exactly when and why the barrier occurred. Their answers were more effective than a simple satisfaction score. One group prioritised convenience, another required clear instructions, and a third group asked for enough time to become familiar with the change.

The revised approach was to show daily patterns in a simple display. A second decision was to explain readings with familiar comparisons. Over the next four weeks, participation increased and fewer residents asked staff for emergency help. Several inexpensive adjustments together created the better result.

In the organiser’s view, the lasting lesson was simple: data has value only when residents can interpret it. An idea may appear excellent in a meeting and still create unnecessary barriers in practice. Careful observation gives residents a chance to improve an idea without abandoning its purpose. Success then becomes easier to define: not as perfect agreement, but as a service that more residents can use with confidence. The experience also reminded those involved that small practical details can strongly influence whether a good idea works. Rather than making quick claims, the coordinators continued to collect comments and adjust the programme carefully. The display now includes a plain-language colour key, exact measurement time and a telephone number for residents who need help interpreting unusual readings.

sections.title: 阅读 A · 36—40
sections.text:
When Martin first became involved with the workplace lunch scheme, the plan was to offer one fixed healthy menu. The early suggestion seemed workable and attracted early support. Observation during the trial showed that staff with different shifts arrived after popular dishes were gone. The underlying aim still had value. It showed that the organisers had understood the goal more clearly than the daily experience of the people expected to take part.

The team therefore decided to allow smaller portions and advance choices. They also agreed to record demand for two weeks before revising menus. During the following month, participation increased and fewer people asked staff for emergency help. A set of small revisions, rather than costly equipment, produced the improvement.

The most serious difficulty was that unused large portions increased waste. Rather than insisting on the draft, Martin invited users to describe exactly when and why the difficulty occurred. Their answers were more useful than a simple satisfaction score. Some people valued convenience, others needed clear instructions, and several wanted enough time to become familiar with the change.

The evidence had clear limits. The revised system did not suit everyone, and the organisers continued to offer an alternative. They also avoided treating the first month's increase as final proof. Seasonal habits and publicity could both affect the figures.

In the organiser’s view, the lasting lesson was simple: healthy services must also be convenient and flexible. A project can sound excellent in a meeting and still create unnecessary barriers in practice. Careful observation gives people a chance to improve an idea without abandoning its purpose. It also makes success easier to define: not as perfect agreement, but as a service that more people can use with confidence. The experience also reminded those involved that small practical details can strongly influence whether a good idea works. Rather than making quick claims, the organisers continued to collect comments and adjust the project carefully. Kitchen staff weigh leftovers by dish and shift, allowing portion decisions to reflect evidence rather than the loudest request received during lunch.

sections.title: 阅读 B · 41—45
sections.text:
Five residents discuss a plan for an evening community gym.

Anna: Hospital shifts finish after the current closing time. A later session twice a week would give workers like me a realistic chance to exercise. Midnight opening is unnecessary; one dependable slot would help.

Ben: Longer hours need trained instructors, cleaners and security staff. Asking today's team to remain late without extra pay would make the service unsafe. Funding and rotas belong in the proposal.

Clara: A winter fitness trial attracted few people until posters appeared in clinics and bus shelters. Numbers rose the next week. Organisers cannot measure demand when likely users have never heard about the offer.

David: My neighbourhood loses its bus service at 7:15. A 9 p.m. class sounds generous but leaves me without transport home. A community minibus or an earlier alternative would widen access.

Eva: Music from group classes makes quiet rehabilitation difficult. I welcome new sessions, provided one area remains calm for people following individual recovery plans. Shared facilities should support different needs.

The proposal therefore involves schedules, staff, publicity, travel and use of space. Counting possible members alone will not settle those questions. The trial can then be revised using evidence instead of assumptions about who exercises and why. Results will be discussed at an open meeting. The council suggests testing Tuesday and Thursday opening for eight weeks. Entry would be booked in forty-five-minute periods so overcrowding can be measured. Participants would note whether they used machines, a class or rehabilitation space. The building contains a lift, changing rooms and twenty bicycle stands, but the nearest bus stop is a fifteen-minute walk away. A small morning session will continue throughout the trial. This gives people who dislike evening travel another option and provides figures for comparison. At the end, the council should publish staffing costs, attendance by time and comments from people who wished to attend but could not.

sections.title: 阅读 C · 46—55
sections.text:
Creating a neighbourhood walking map takes [46] planning. Routes must be [47] for intended users, while [48] checks keep information accurate. Signs [49] distances and warnings, and printed copies should remain [50] to residents without smartphones.

Early maps showed little [51] with local travel habits. The team then organised [52] guided walks and changed several routes to [53] road crossings. These events [54] residents to [55] in testing the map.

Older walkers identified benches that had disappeared, and parents marked paths wide enough for pushchairs. Volunteers timed routes at different speeds instead of publishing one unrealistic figure. They also distinguished well-lit evening paths from attractive daytime shortcuts. A revised edition uses larger symbols and names the nearest bus stop at each starting point. Weather can still alter a path, so users are invited to report temporary problems. The map's usefulness comes from lived experience as much as measurement. By reviewing it each season, the group provides guidance that is clear, current and responsive to different bodies and routines. Each route includes an emergency contact point. Volunteers check damaged signs after storms and update the website before printing a new seasonal edition. The printed and online versions use the same symbols, and every suggested change is checked by two walkers. Schools have requested copies for travel lessons. Local doctors also distribute the map when gentle activity may help a patient.

sections.title: 写作 · 56

chart.title: the percentage of residents walking to work at least twice a week

questions.prompt: Write an essay of about 120 words based on the chart. Describe and interpret the chart briefly, and give your comments.
questions.explanation: 先概括五年总体趋势并引用起止数据，再解释可能原因，最后给出个人评价和一至两项可行建议。

sections.model: The chart shows changes in the percentage of residents walking to work at least twice a week over five years. Overall, the figure moved steadily from 12% in 2021 to 43% in 2025. The clearest change occurred in the middle of the period, suggesting that more people gradually accepted this choice. In my view, the trend is encouraging because it reflects greater attention to convenient and responsible daily habits. However, rising numbers alone do not guarantee a good experience. Organisers should maintain reliable facilities, publish simple guidance and collect feedback from different users. They should also keep an alternative for people who cannot use the service easily. With careful management, the positive trend can continue and bring lasting value to the wider community.
